title: Count Non-Decreasing Subarrays After K Operations
summary: Given an array of integers and an integer k, determine the count of subarrays that can become non-decreasing by applying at most k increment operations to any element within each subarray.
statement: Given an array of integers and an integer k, determine the count of subarrays that can become non-decreasing by applying at most k increment operations to any element within each subarray. An array is non-decreasing if each element is greater than or equal to the previous one.
constraints: nums has up to 100,000 positive values and k is positive.
Within each chosen subarray, one operation increments one element by one.
Count subarrays requiring at most k operations to become non-decreasing.
hints: For a fixed left boundary, the minimum increments equal the area needed to raise values to successive prefix maxima.
Scan leftward with a monotonic block deque and shrink the right edge while cost exceeds k.
Merge lower prefix-max blocks when adding a left value; subtract the rightmost block height gap when removing right.
The deque represents the exact raised profile, and cost monotonicity makes every shorter suffix of a feasible window feasible.
editorial: The deque represents the exact raised profile, and cost monotonicity makes every shorter suffix of a feasible window feasible.

tests.explanation: Seventeen subarrays can be raised to non-decreasing order within seven increments.
The singletons and subarray [3,2] qualify, giving four.
